items.title: Kong AI Gateway 2.0 reaches general availability
items.summary: The production-supported release reduces product-execution risk around Kong's AI-control-plane strategy. It strengthens the product-position score, while valuation inputs remain unchanged until commercial traction or financial contribution is disclosed.
confirmed: Kong says AI Gateway 2.0 is generally available and production-supported in Konnect with its own runtime and control plane.

The release adds MCP Server Bundling with per-caller tool visibility, modality-aware cost governance, Kong Identity principals, expanded model-provider support, and native AWS IAM authentication for Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.
uncertain: Kong did not disclose customer adoption, bookings, incremental ARR, pricing, margins, or financial contribution.
The pace of customer migration from existing Gateway AI plugins to the standalone product is unknown.

items.title: Kong centers its 2026 strategy on AI connectivity
items.summary: The strategy reinforces Kong's position as a control layer for APIs and AI traffic, but it does not supply the audited growth, margin, retention, or share-count evidence needed for a valuation upgrade.
confirmed: Kong described AI connectivity, large-enterprise adoption, organizational expansion, and regional investment as strategic priorities.
uncertain: Revenue contribution, adoption rates, growth, and margin effects were not disclosed.

items.title: OpenMeter adds usage metering and billing to Kong's platform
items.summary: The acquisition broadens Kong's monetization layer for API and AI workloads. It improves strategic breadth, while integration quality and financial contribution remain unproven.
confirmed: Kong acquired OpenMeter and described native usage metering and billing as part of the expanded platform.
uncertain: Purchase terms, integration economics, customer uptake, and incremental ARR were not disclosed.
